title: Rule 4(1) — Duties of E-Commerce Entities
text: Every e-commerce entity shall be a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956 or the Companies Act, 2013 or a foreign company or an office, branch or agency outside India owned or controlled by a person resident in India; and appoint a nodal person of contact or an alternate senior designated functionary who is resident in India, to ensure compliance with the provisions of the Act or the rules made thereunder.

title: Rule 4(2) — Grievance Officer & Complaint Redressal Timelines
text: Every e-commerce entity shall establish an adequate grievance redressal mechanism having regard to the number of grievances and designate a grievance officer for consumer grievance redressal on its portal and publish the name, contact details and designation of such officer. The Grievance Officer shall acknowledge the receipt of any consumer complaint within forty-eight hours and redresses the complaint within one month from the date of receipt of the complaint.

title: Rule 4(4) — Information & Transparency to Consumers
text: Every e-commerce entity shall provide clear and accessible information on its platform regarding refund, exchange, warranty and guarantee, delivery and shipment, modes of payment, and grievance redressal mechanism, in a clear and accessible manner to its users at the appropriate stage of the transaction.

title: Rule 5(3) — Marketplace Disclosures on Return, Refund and Delivery
text: Every marketplace e-commerce entity shall provide to its users in a clear and accessible manner on its platform details about return, refund, exchange, warranty and guarantee, delivery and shipment, and any other similar information which may be required by consumers to make informed decisions. Marketplace e-commerce entities must also provide information regarding mechanisms for consumer grievance redressal including ticket numbers for tracking.

title: Rule 6(2) — Sellers Duties regarding Return, Defective Goods and Refund
text: No seller on a marketplace e-commerce entity shall refuse to take back goods, or withdraw or discontinue services purchased or agreed to be purchased, or refuse to refund consideration paid, if such goods or services are defective, deficient or spurious, or if the characteristics or features of the goods or services are not as represented or if such goods or services are delivered late from the stated delivery schedule: Provided that such refusal may be justified if late delivery is due to force majeure.

title: Rule 7 — Duties of Inventory E-Commerce Entities
text: Every inventory e-commerce entity shall not refuse to take back goods, or withdraw or discontinue services, or refuse to refund consideration paid, if such goods or services are defective, deficient, spurious, or if the goods or services delivered are different from what was represented or delivered late beyond the promised delivery schedule. Inventory e-commerce entities must process all legitimate refund requests within a reasonable period as prescribed under applicable laws.
